From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: deployment mode & sizing clarifications from today's call

Alex — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and a couple of concrete asks so we can size a Reserved GPU recommendation for NimbleHealth: 

Summary from call:
- Primary requirement: low-latency document summarization for clinician notes (95th pctl latency target ~120ms).
- Expected production TPS: 60 concurrent inference requests at peak, estimated 20 requests/sec sustained during business hours.
- Typical token mix: short prompts (avg 120 tokens input) + long completions (avg 650 tokens output) — you mentioned a 4:1 read:write ratio.
- Data requirements: VPC private deployment considered, but initial preference is Dedicated (reserved pool) in our US region for isolation + predictable throughput.

Asks / clarifications we need to finalize a SKU matrix and cost estimate: 
1) Can you confirm whether the 60 concurrent figure is concurrent sessions or parallel active inferences? (I.e., are you holding open sessions with long waits between tokens or are most requests short-lived?)
2) Please attach a sample traffic CSV (timestamps, prompt tokens, completion tokens) if you have one — that will let us model actual KV cache benefits.
3) Any hard SLA requirements for uptime/maintenance windows beyond standard 99.9%?

Next steps from our side:
- I'll loop in Ben (inference ops) and Karthik (solutions) to draft a 2-option Reserved SKU recommendation: a cost-optimized baseline and a latency-optimized baseline.
- If you can share the traffic snapshot, we'll run an internal run-rate sim and send back a recommended GPU mix (flavors + counts) and expected 95th pctl latencies.

Attach: please send the traffic snapshot when convenient (nimble_traffic_snapshot.csv suggested format).

Thanks —
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 (415) 555-0193

Evelyn / team — I ran a quick simulation on Alex's CSV and sketched two conservative Reserved-pool options below. I've attached a short playbook PDF (redwood_reserved_sku_playbook.pdf) with assumptions and cost bands.

Summary of assumptions used in the sim:
- Request profile: avg input 120 tokens / avg completion 650 tokens; median inference time per token on H100-like flavor ~0.8ms/token when batched; A100-like ~1.3ms/token.
- Batching: continuous batching enabled with target batch windows set to 8–12ms to preserve latency SLOs.
- KV cache: small prefix reuse observed (10–12% saved tokens) since prompts are relatively stable across clinicians.
- Concurrency: target 60 active inferences at peak; we model three concurrency slices (30/60/90) for safety.

Option A — Cost-optimized (baseline):
- Hardware: mix of A100-equivalent 80GB x 6 GPUs
- Expected 95th pctl latency: ~180–220ms at 60 concurrency (depends on request burstiness)
- Monthly reserved commit: ~$XX,XXX (ballpark; see playbook for cost bands)
- Notes: Good token throughput, cheaper per-GPU unit, higher latency tail under bursty traffic.

Option B — Latency-optimized (performance):
- Hardware: H100-equivalent 80GB x 4 GPUs (higher single-GPU throughput)
- Expected 95th pctl latency: ~100–140ms at 60 concurrency (with continuous batching tuned)
- Monthly reserved commit: ~$YY,YYY (premium)
- Notes: Better headroom for longer completions and spiky bursts; recommended if 120ms 95th pctl is a hard requirement.

Migration note (Dedicated -> Private VPC/on-prem):
- Both options are compatible with a future Private VPC migration; main work is networking/KMS and customer IT ops handoff. No model artifact changes expected. For air-gapped on-prem, estimate +3–4 engineer-weeks for packaging and validation (depends on customer infra).

Deliverables attached: redwood_reserved_sku_playbook.pdf (assumptions, raw sim outputs, recommended next steps)

Next steps / asks back to Alex / procurement:
- Confirm whether 120ms 95th pctl is a firm requirement or a target.
- Procurement: any contracting constraints we should be aware of (PO cadence, required terms, security questionnaire timeline).
- If Alex wants the lower-latency option, we'll re-run sims to size for 99th pctl as well.

I can turn these into an email-ready deliverable for Procurement once Alex confirms the SLA target.

Ben Carter
Principal, Inference Operations — Redwood Inference
